transcript:
00:00:00 - Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, AE for Lumen. Quick intro, Ethan from our SE team is on to cover the technicals.
00:00:08 - Priya Natarajan: Hi Ava, thanks, Priya here, CISO at Lumen Finance, with Marcus and Sara. We have a lot to cover around encryption and keys.
00:00:18 - Ethan Cole: Great, hi all. We'll focus on encryption in transit and at rest, BYOK workflows, HSM support, and audit logging. Feel free to interrupt.
00:00:27 - Marcus Lee: Quick note on constraints: we operate in multiple regions and have strict residency for EU and APAC customers. We also have an internal KMS and policies that require bring-your-own-key for certain data categories.
00:00:38 - Ava Martinez: Understood. High level, Redwood encrypts all traffic in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and data at rest with AES-256. For hosted customers we default to Redwood-managed keys, but we support BYOK and HSM-backed keys for dedicated/private deployments.
00:00:54 - Priya Natarajan: When you say HSM-backed, do you integrate with cloud HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM) or do you have your own? We need FIPS 140-2 level 3 assurances for some vaulting.
00:01:07 - Ethan Cole: We integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM providers — AWS KMS with CloudHSM, Google Cloud KMS with HSM, and Azure Key Vault HSM. For private deployments we can support HSM appliances as part of the on-prem package. Our attestation for HSM usage maps to FIPS guidance; we'll share the specifics in the security pack.
00:01:28 - Sara Cho: Also interested in the BYOK lifecycle: creation, revocation, rotation, who has access, and audit trails.
00:01:36 - Ethan Cole: Right. Typical pattern is envelope encryption: customer master key (CMK) in their KMS encrypts per-tenant data encryption keys (DEKs) that Redwood stores encrypted. DEKs are used for efficient at-rest encryption. Rotation is handled by re-wrapping DEKs with a new CMK version — that can be automated or manual depending on customer policy.
00:01:58 - Marcus Lee: Do you support key import into CloudHSM so the key material never leaves our control, or are you relying on KMS-generated keys? We need the import option for regulatory reasons.
00:02:08 - Ethan Cole: Yes, where the cloud provider supports key import (e.g., AWS CloudHSM/FIPS import workflows) you can import key material and we can use it via the KMS API. For on-prem HSMs we support PKCS#11 interfaces for integration.
00:02:20 - Priya Natarajan: How about access control for key usage? We need separation of duties — devs shouldn't be able to decrypt raw records.
00:02:29 - Ava Martinez: We enforce least-privilege via RBAC at the platform level, and key policies live in the customer's KMS. Typically the Redwood service principal has Encrypt/Decrypt permissions scoped to the CMK. For additional separation, you can use two-person approve flows in your KMS or hardware HSM policies.
00:02:47 - Diego Alvarez: Do you provide fine-grained logging for key usage? We need cryptographic operations logged to tie back to audit events.
00:02:55 - Ethan Cole: Key usage events are emitted by the KMS (CloudTrail for AWS, Audit Logs for GCP) and we surface request-level audit logs in Redwood Console that reference the KMS operation IDs. We also keep request metadata — timestamp, route, model, tenant ID — in an append-only audit store. Note: retention policies and PII in logs are configurable per customer.
00:03:22 - Priya Natarajan: What's the usual retention for those logs? Compliance sometimes demands seven years for certain records.
00:03:29 - Ava Martinez: By default we retain detailed request logs for 90 days in the console and can export to the customer's long-term storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) for arbitrary retention. For enterprise/private we can set up direct streaming to your SIEM to meet multi-year retention.
00:03:46 - Marcus Lee: If we stream to our SIEM, what about log integrity? We need tamper-evident storage for some records.
00:03:53 - Ethan Cole: We support append-only storage and can ship logs with checksums; when paired with your object store's immutability features (e.g., S3 Object Lock) you get tamper-evidence. We can also provide signed log bundles on request for audits.
00:04:12 - Sara Cho: Let's go deeper on key rotation. If we rotate a CMK, what is the effect on tokens, sessions, and live inferences? Any downtime or re-encryption windows?
00:04:23 - Ethan Cole: With envelope encryption, DEKs remain unchanged until you rewrap them. Rewrapping is non-blocking; you can rewrap in background and there shouldn't be downtime. For in-flight KV cache (token-level caches on model runtime), we keep cache encryption separate and version it — a rotation will require cache rewraps but we have a graceful fallback to prior key versions during the transition to avoid errors.
00:04:47 - Diego Alvarez: You mentioned KV cache — can we restrict where those caches live? Some caches contain contextual prefixes that are sensitive.
00:04:54 - Ava Martinez: In Dedicated/Private modes KV caches live on your dedicated nodes within your VPC or on-prem hardware. For hosted multi-tenant we follow strict isolation; but if you need absolute control, Dedicated or Private deployment is recommended.
00:05:07 - Priya Natarajan: For the BYOK onboarding, what's the operational process? We want minimal operational burden, but we need to own key material.
00:05:16 - Ethan Cole: Typical process: 1) We send an onboarding checklist; 2) You provision a CMK in your KMS or import key material; 3) You create a key policy granting the Redwood service principal limited Encrypt/Decrypt; 4) We test encrypt/decrypt and verify audit logs; 5) Pilot starts. We'll share a sample key policy and automation scripts.
00:05:36 - Marcus Lee: Will we have to rotate keys on both sides? Meaning, if we rotate in our KMS, will you need to update something?
00:05:43 - Ethan Cole: Rotation in your KMS is visible via key versioning; our rewrap automation will detect new key versions via the KMS API. We'll coordinate with you for any forced rewraps. If you revoke access entirely, Redwood will failover to configured fallback keys per the agreed policy, but that might cause service errors until resolved.
00:06:01 - Priya Natarajan: How do you handle backup and disaster recovery for encrypted data?
00:06:07 - Ava Martinez: Encrypted backups are stored encrypted with the same envelope approach. Backup keys are managed in the same KMS. For DR, we can replicate encrypted backups cross-region per your policy; key access is necessary in the target region or you can import keys into the target KMS to allow decryption.
00:06:22 - Sara Cho: Is there a documented SLA for key-based operations or HA for KMS calls? We worry about KMS throttling or outages causing latency spikes.
00:06:31 - Ethan Cole: We treat KMS calls as critical and cache DEKs to minimize per-request KMS calls. For HA we support multi-region CMKs and retry/backoff patterns. For enterprise Dedicated we can set up local HSMs to avoid cross-region KMS latency. We also have fallback policies to use a secondary key store if primary is unavailable, but that requires pre-approval to ensure compliance.
00:06:55 - Marcus Lee: One more on compliance: do you have SOC 2 and ISO27001 certs? Our procurement needs the reports and may require an in-person audit or virtual review.
00:07:06 - Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. We'll share the reports under NDA and can coordinate a virtual walkthrough with our security team.
00:07:15 - Priya Natarajan: Good. Can you also confirm encryption of data in transit between Redwood and any model provider or third-party integrations? We have concerns about data leaving the environment.
00:07:25 - Ethan Cole: All external calls are TLS-encrypted. For third-party model providers we can keep data in our runtime; if we call external endpoints we annotate and require outbound routing policies. In Dedicated/Private you can disable outbound model fetches and only use pinned models in your environment.
00:07:44 - Diego Alvarez: On the network side, do you support PrivateLink/VPC Peering or similar for hosted connections? We prefer PrivateLink to avoid public endpoints.
00:07:52 - Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering patterns for inbound traffic. For Dedicated, we can colocate inside your VPC using VPC endpoints. For private on-prem we use direct connect/MPLS setups per customer.
00:08:06 - Marcus Lee: About logs, can we get per-tenant keyed logs that exclude prompt text or PII? We need to segregate telemetry and sensitive content.
00:08:15 - Ethan Cole: Yes, log filters can redact prompt content; you can choose level of detail exported. For compliance we can store hashed or redacted prompt content, and full transcripts can be stored in your encrypted object store if required.
00:08:29 - Priya Natarajan: Any certifications around cryptographic libraries or FIPS modules used? We require FIPS-validated modules for certain workloads.
00:08:37 - Ava Martinez: Our platform can be configured to run with FIPS-validated crypto modules in Private/Dedicated deployments. We'll include the module versions and audit references in the security pack.
00:08:47 - Sara Cho: From a legal perspective, we might want a clause around key custody and if Redwood will ever have access to cleartext.
00:08:55 - Ava Martinez: Standard is that if Customer manages CMKs and never shares key material, Redwood cannot access cleartext. We'll work with Legal on contract language — e.g., key custody, destructive termination procedures, and escrow arrangements if needed.
00:09:09 - Ethan Cole: Also to note, for debugging we sometimes request access to redacted traces; those are controlled by your RBAC and require approval. We can provide a redaction-first workflow.
00:09:20 - Marcus Lee: Practical question: for the pilot, can we run a small data set with BYOK and measure latency impact? We need to compare Redwood-managed keys vs BYOK in our region.
00:09:30 - Ava Martinez: Absolutely. Pilot scope: baseline with Redwood-managed keys, then BYOK with your KMS in the same region to measure KMS call latency and overall token latencies. We'll instrument with per-token timing and KMS call metrics.
00:09:43 - Priya Natarajan: If BYOK adds latency, how do you mitigate? Also concerns about cost of KMS calls at scale.
00:09:51 - Ethan Cole: We mitigate via DEK caching, batching KMS operations during rotate windows, and minimizing synchronous KMS calls on the hot path. For extreme scale we recommend Dedicated/Private with local HSM to reduce network overhead. Cost-wise, DR and KMS usage can be profiled — we'll include cost simulations in the pilot.
00:10:07 - Diego Alvarez: Are there any known gotchas with key policies that we should watch for? For example, account vs principal scoping causing accidental broad access.
00:10:15 - Ethan Cole: Yes, common issues: overly broad key policies, forgetting to scope to specific service principals or ARNs, and not including cross-account use statements when using cross-account roles. We'll provide a sample key policy tightened to minimum privileges.
00:10:28 - Ava Martinez: I'm going to share a sample key policy and onboarding checklist after the call.
00:10:33 - Priya Natarajan: Good. Also, slightly separate topic: do you have session-level encryption for model responses, or is it all at-rest and in-transit? We want to ensure ephemeral keys for real-time sessions.
00:10:44 - Ethan Cole: We support ephemeral session keys for sensitive workloads. Session keys are derived and rotated frequently and used for session-level caches. That's part of our Dedicated/Private offering typically.
00:10:56 - Marcus Lee: Okay, sounds promising. Let's talk about documentation and artifacts you promised.
00:11:01 - Ava Martinez: We'll attach the security pack (SOC2/ISO certs), BYOK/HSM integration guide, sample KMS policies, and a pilot runbook. Expect an email with links by end of day.
00:11:10 - Sara Cho: One last legal ask: please include sample contract language for key custody and breach notification timelines.
00:11:18 - Ava Martinez: Noted — we'll include typical SLRs and notification timelines.
00:11:22 - Priya Natarajan: Great. Should we set the next meeting to review the pilot scope and technical runbook?
00:11:29 - Ava Martinez: Yes, how about week of April 13th?
00:11:33 - Marcus Lee: Works for infra.
00:11:35 - Priya Natarajan: Works for security.
00:11:37 - Ava Martinez: I'll send a calendar invite. Quick recap: Redwood to share certs + security pack; SE to share BYOK guide + key policy; Lumen to provide region/residency list and retention requirements. Pilot kickoff week of April 13th.
00:11:50 - Priya Natarajan: Thanks everyone.
00:11:52 - Ethan Cole: Thanks, bye.
00:11:54 - Ava Martinez: Bye all.
